title: The line graph below shows electricity generation from three sources in a country between 2000 and 2020.
overview: Gas stayed the leading source throughout, while coal and solar both expanded, with solar growing fastest in the final decade.

band7.answer:
The line graph illustrates how much electricity a country generated from gas, coal and solar power between 2000 and 2020, measured in thousand gigawatt hours.

Overall, gas remained the dominant source throughout the period, although coal and solar power both grew considerably. Solar was the least significant source in every year.

In 2000, gas produced 18 thousand gigawatt hours, compared with only 3 for coal and none for solar. Gas output then rose steadily, reaching 32 in 2010 and peaking at 41 in 2020, which was more than double its starting figure.

Coal followed a different pattern. It increased slightly from 3 in 2000 to 6 in 2010, but then climbed sharply to 14 in 2015 and 22 in 2020. Solar generation was negligible at first, standing at just 1 in 2005 and 2 in 2010. However, it then grew rapidly, rising to 5 in 2015 and 12 in 2020. Despite this growth, solar remained well below the other two sources by the end of the period.
band7.comment: Clear overview and accurate data selection, with a logical split between sources. Vocabulary is sound but less varied than at Band 8.

band8.answer:
The line graph compares electricity generation from gas, coal and solar power in one country over a twenty-year period, from 2000 to 2020, in thousand gigawatt hours.

Overall, gas was consistently the largest contributor, whereas coal and solar, which began from very low bases, both expanded markedly, with solar showing the steepest proportional growth.

Gas output rose steadily from 18 thousand gigawatt hours in 2000 to 25 in 2005 and 32 in 2010, before increasing more gradually to 38 in 2015 and reaching a high of 41 in 2020. Overall, this represented an increase of more than 120 per cent.

Coal generation was initially minimal at 3, edging up to 4 in 2005 and 6 in 2010. After 2010, however, it accelerated dramatically, more than doubling to 14 in 2015 and climbing further to 22 by 2020. Solar power did not register at all in 2000, and contributed merely 1 and 2 in 2005 and 2010 respectively. Growth then picked up considerably, with output reaching 5 in 2015 and 12 in 2020, although this still fell well short of both rival sources.
band8.comment: Precise figures, controlled comparison and well-chosen linking devices throughout. A wider range of trend language lifts the answer to Band 8.

title: The bar chart below shows the average monthly amount that urban and rural households in Bangladesh spent on five food categories in 2022.
overview: Urban households spent more on most food items, especially fish and meat, while rice was the main expense only for rural families.
key_features: Fish and meat is the largest urban expense
Rice is the largest rural expense
Edible oil and pulses cost least in both areas

band7.answer:
The bar chart compares how much urban and rural households in Bangladesh spent each month on five categories of food in 2022.

Overall, city families spent more than village families on four of the five items, and the biggest difference was in fish and meat. Rice was the only category where rural households paid more, and it was their largest single expense.

Looking at the main items, urban households spent 3,600 BDT on fish and meat, which was clearly the highest figure for cities, whereas rural households spent only 2,400 BDT on the same category. Rice accounted for 2,800 BDT in urban areas but 3,100 BDT in rural areas. Vegetables also showed a gap, with 1,500 BDT in cities against 1,200 BDT in the countryside.

The two cheapest categories were edible oil and pulses. Urban households paid 900 BDT for oil and 600 BDT for pulses, while the equivalent rural figures were slightly lower at 800 BDT and 500 BDT. These small differences suggest that spending on basic staples was fairly similar in both settings.
band7.comment: Clear overview and accurate figures with sensible grouping. Vocabulary is adequate but less varied than a band 8 response.

band8.answer:
The bar chart illustrates average monthly household expenditure on five food categories in urban and rural Bangladesh in 2022.

Overall, urban households outspent their rural counterparts on every item except rice, and the widest gap appeared in fish and meat. While animal protein was the single largest cost for city dwellers, rice dominated rural food budgets.

Fish and meat cost urban families 3,600 BDT a month, 1,200 BDT more than the 2,400 BDT recorded in rural areas, making it the most striking contrast in the chart. Rice moved in the opposite direction: rural households devoted 3,100 BDT to it, compared with 2,800 BDT in towns and cities, a difference of 300 BDT. Spending on vegetables was also higher in urban areas, at 1,500 BDT as opposed to 1,200 BDT.

Expenditure on the remaining two categories was modest in both settings. Urban households paid 900 BDT for edible oil and 600 BDT for pulses, whereas rural households paid slightly less, at 800 BDT and 500 BDT respectively. Pulses were therefore the cheapest item in each area, costing roughly one fifth of what was spent on rice.
band8.comment: Precise comparisons, calculated differences and a strong overview give excellent task achievement. Cohesion and lexical range are wider than at band 7.

title: The line graph below shows the number of people using mobile banking services in urban and rural areas of Bangladesh between 2018 and 2023.
instruction: Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
overview: Both groups of users grew steadily, but rural usage rose far faster and almost caught up with urban usage by 2023.
key_features: Both lines rise throughout the period
Rural growth is much steeper than urban growth
The gap narrows from 9 million to 4 million

band7.answer:
The line graph illustrates how many people used mobile banking services in the urban and rural areas of Bangladesh from 2018 to 2023, with figures given in millions.

Overall, the number of users rose steadily in both areas, but the increase was much sharper in rural areas, which almost caught up with urban areas by the end of the period.

In 2018, 18 million urban residents used mobile banking, double the rural figure of 9 million. Urban numbers then grew to 24 million in 2019 and 33 million in 2020, before reaching 41 million in 2021.

Rural usage climbed more quickly after 2019, rising from 13 million to 30 million in 2021. By 2022, there were 48 million urban users and 40 million rural users, and in 2023 the figures reached 54 million and 50 million respectively, leaving a gap of only 4 million. Overall, rural usage grew by 41 million over the period, whereas urban usage grew by 36 million, so the rural group was clearly the faster-growing one.
band7.comment: The answer has a clear overview and reports the key figures accurately. Band 8 would add more precise comparisons, such as the size of the gap each year.

band8.answer:
The line graph compares the number of mobile banking users in urban and rural Bangladesh over a six-year period from 2018 to 2023, measured in millions.

Overall, usage increased consistently in both settings, yet the rural segment expanded far more rapidly, so that the initial advantage held by urban areas had almost disappeared by 2023.

Urban users began at 18 million in 2018, exactly twice the rural total of 9 million. The urban figure then increased by 6 million in 2019 and by a further 9 million in 2020, reaching 33 million, before growth slowed to around 7 million a year, ending at 54 million in 2023.

By contrast, rural usage more than tripled in the first four years, from 9 million to 30 million in 2021. The most striking rise occurred between 2021 and 2022, when it jumped by 10 million to 40 million. A final increase of 10 million took the rural total to 50 million, just 4 million below the urban figure. In total, rural usage rose by 41 million, compared with an urban increase of 36 million.
band8.comment: Precise figures, calculated differences and a clear contrast between the two groups make this a strong response. Cohesion and range of comparative language are both very good.

title: The line graph below shows the number of students enrolled in three university subject areas between 2010 and 2022.
overview: Engineering enrolment rose the most and overtook business, while arts was the only subject to decline.

band7.answer:
The line graph shows how many students enrolled in engineering, business and arts courses at universities between 2010 and 2022, in thousands.

Overall, engineering and business both attracted more students over the period, whereas arts was the only subject to decline. Engineering showed the greatest growth and ended as the most popular subject.

In 2010, business was the most popular field with 55 thousand students, followed by engineering at 40 thousand and arts at 35 thousand. Business numbers then grew to 70 thousand in 2013 and peaked at 88 thousand in 2019, before falling slightly to 85 thousand in 2022.

Engineering rose consistently throughout the period. Enrolment went from 40 thousand to 48 thousand in 2013, then to 60 thousand in 2016 and 75 thousand in 2019. By 2022 it had reached 90 thousand, overtaking business after 2019. In contrast, arts enrolment fell gradually from 35 thousand in 2010 to 30 thousand in 2016 and just 22 thousand in 2022, making it the least popular subject by the end.
band7.comment: Good coverage of all three subjects with accurate figures and a clear overview. The paragraphing is logical, though the comparisons could be more varied.

band8.answer:
The line graph illustrates changes in the number of students enrolled in engineering, business and arts at universities over a twelve-year period, from 2010 to 2022, with figures given in thousands.

Overall, engineering experienced the strongest and most consistent growth, eventually surpassing business, while arts was the only subject to see a persistent decline.

In 2010, business led with 55 thousand enrolments, comfortably ahead of engineering on 40 thousand and arts on 35 thousand. Business then rose rapidly to 70 thousand in 2013 and 82 thousand in 2016, levelling off at 88 thousand in 2019 before dipping marginally to 85 thousand in 2022.

Engineering, by contrast, grew at a steady pace in every period, climbing from 40 thousand to 48 thousand, 60 thousand and 75 thousand by 2019. It then reached 90 thousand in 2022, which meant it had overtaken business after 2019 and more than doubled its original figure. Arts moved in the opposite direction, slipping from 35 thousand to 34 thousand in 2013 and 30 thousand in 2016, and bottoming out at 22 thousand by 2022, the lowest of the three subjects.
band8.comment: Accurate and precise, with effective use of contrast and a clear sense of ranking changes. Varied sentence structures and trend vocabulary support the higher band.

title: The bar chart below shows the number of students enrolled in five subject areas at Bangladeshi universities in 2010 and 2020.
overview: Enrolment rose in four of the five subjects, with business growing most, while humanities was the only subject to decline.

band7.answer:
The bar chart compares university enrolment in five subject areas in Bangladesh in 2010 and in 2020, measured in thousands of students.

Overall, enrolment increased in every subject apart from humanities, and business recorded the biggest growth. By 2020 business had become the most popular subject by a wide margin.

In 2010, business had 120,000 students and humanities had 110,000, so these two were the largest areas. Over the following decade, business enrolment climbed to 210,000, an increase of 90,000, whereas the number studying humanities fell to 90,000. Engineering also grew significantly, from 85,000 students to 140,000.

Science and medicine were smaller fields. Science enrolment rose only slightly, from 95,000 to 100,000, so it was the most stable subject. Medicine started from the lowest level, at 30,000 students, but it grew to 55,000 by 2020, which was a rise of more than 80 percent. Even so, it remained the smallest of the five areas at the end of the period.
band7.comment: Good selection of key trends with correct data and a clear overview. A few sentences are simple and could show more varied structures.

band8.answer:
The bar chart shows how many students were enrolled in five subject areas at universities in Bangladesh in 2010 and 2020.

Overall, four of the five subjects attracted more students over the decade, with business expanding the most, whereas humanities was the only area to lose students. Business therefore extended its lead as the largest field, while humanities slipped from second place to third.

Business enrolment rose from 120,000 in 2010 to 210,000 in 2020, a gain of 90,000 and by far the largest increase in the chart. Engineering followed a similar upward path, growing from 85,000 to 140,000. In contrast, humanities declined from 110,000 to 90,000, dropping below science by the end of the period.

Science remained almost static, edging up from 95,000 to 100,000 students. Medicine was the smallest subject in both years, yet its enrolment nearly doubled, climbing from 30,000 to 55,000. By 2020, business attracted around four times as many students as medicine and more than twice as many as science, which shows how strongly demand shifted towards commercial courses.
band8.comment: Accurate, well-selected data with insightful comparisons and a precise overview. Flexible grammar and cohesive devices support a high band.

title: The line graph below shows the share of electricity in Bangladesh generated from natural gas, coal and renewable sources between 2000 and 2020.
instruction: Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
overview: Natural gas remained the leading source but declined steadily, while coal and renewables both grew in importance.
key_features: Coal rises most among the alternatives
Renewables are still the smallest source in 2020

band7.answer:
The line graph shows what percentage of Bangladesh's electricity came from natural gas, coal and renewable sources over a twenty-year period, starting in 2000.

Overall, natural gas was the dominant source throughout, although its share fell considerably. In contrast, coal and renewables both became more significant, with coal growing faster.

Natural gas supplied 88 percent of electricity in 2000, and this dropped slightly to 84 percent in 2005 and 78 percent in 2010. The decline then became steeper, with the figure falling to 62 percent in 2015 and 48 percent in 2020.

Coal began at a very low level of just 2 percent and edged up to 3 percent in 2005 and 5 percent in 2010. It then rose sharply to 12 percent in 2015 and 19 percent in 2020. Renewable energy stayed at around 1 to 2 percent until 2010, then increased to 4 percent in 2015 and 9 percent in 2020, remaining the smallest source. Overall, the combined share of coal and renewables in 2020 was 28 percent, compared with only 3 percent in 2000.
band7.comment: All main trends are covered and the data is accurate, with a clear overview. The language could be more varied to reach a higher band.

band8.answer:
The line graph compares the proportions of Bangladesh's electricity produced from natural gas, coal and renewables at five-year intervals between 2000 and 2020.

Overall, natural gas remained the principal source throughout, but its contribution shrank markedly, whereas coal and renewables gained ground, with coal expanding the most.

In 2000, gas accounted for a commanding 88 percent of generation, compared with only 2 percent for coal and 1 percent for renewables. Gas then declined gradually to 78 percent by 2010, before falling more steeply, by 16 points, to 62 percent in 2015 and by a further 14 points to 48 percent in 2020.

Coal followed the opposite pattern. Its share crept up from 2 percent to 5 percent over the first decade, then climbed to 12 percent in 2015 and 19 percent in 2020, almost four times its 2010 level. Renewables remained marginal at 1 to 2 percent until 2010 but rose to 4 percent in 2015 and 9 percent in 2020, still well below coal. Taken together, coal and renewables supplied 28 percent in 2020, up from just 3 percent two decades earlier.
band8.comment: The answer uses precise figures and calculated changes to support clear trends. Varied vocabulary for rises and falls shows strong lexical control.

title: The line graph below shows the average number of daily passengers using three forms of public transport in a city between 2012 and 2022.
overview: Buses carried by far the most passengers, trains grew overall, and ferries lost ground, with all three hit in 2020.

band7.answer:
The line graph compares the average number of passengers per day who used buses, trains and ferries in a city between 2012 and 2022, in thousands.

Overall, buses were by far the most widely used form of transport, while ferries were the least used. All three modes dropped in 2020, but only trains finished the period higher than they started.

Bus travel began at 520 thousand passengers in 2012 and rose to a peak of 560 thousand in 2016. It then fell to 545 thousand in 2018 and dropped sharply to 430 thousand in 2020, before recovering to 500 thousand in 2022.

Trains were much less popular, with 120 thousand passengers in 2012. This figure grew steadily to 170 thousand in 2018, fell to 110 thousand in 2020, and then rebounded to 175 thousand in 2022, its highest level. Ferry use was lower still, decreasing from 80 thousand in 2012 to 70 thousand in 2018 and 50 thousand in 2020. It recovered slightly to 65 thousand by 2022, which was still below the starting figure.
band7.comment: The overview captures the key trends and the 2020 dip, and the data is accurate. Some repetition of structure keeps it at Band 7.

band8.answer:
The line graph details how many passengers used buses, trains and ferries in a city on an average day between 2012 and 2022, measured in thousands.

Overall, buses consistently carried far more passengers than the other two modes. Although every form of transport suffered a sharp fall in 2020, only trains ended the period with a higher figure than at the outset.

Bus patronage rose gradually from 520 thousand in 2012 to a high of 560 thousand in 2016, then eased to 545 thousand in 2018. A steep decline followed, to 430 thousand in 2020, but numbers recovered to 500 thousand by 2022, still below the earlier peak.

Trains showed the strongest overall growth. Starting at 120 thousand, the figure climbed steadily to 135 thousand in 2014, 150 thousand in 2016 and 170 thousand in 2018. After plunging to 110 thousand in 2020, it rebounded to 175 thousand, the highest of any year. Ferries, meanwhile, were the least popular and in long-term decline, slipping from 80 thousand to 70 thousand by 2018 and falling to 50 thousand in 2020, before a modest recovery to 65 thousand in 2022.
band8.comment: Excellent control of detail and contrast, with a strong overview that identifies the exceptional mode. Vocabulary for change is varied and accurate.

title: The bar chart below shows the percentage of people in different age groups in Bangladesh who used the internet on a mobile phone in 2018 and 2023.
overview: Mobile internet use rose in every age group, with younger people the heaviest users and the oldest group the lightest in both years.
key_features: Youngest group highest in both years

band7.answer:
The bar chart compares the proportion of people in five age groups who used the internet on a mobile phone in Bangladesh in 2018 and 2023.

Overall, mobile internet use rose in every age group, and younger people were always more likely to be online than older people. The 16-24 group had the highest figures in both years, while people aged 55 and over had the lowest.

In 2018, 48 percent of those aged 16-24 used mobile internet, and this rose to 82 percent in 2023. The 25-34 group followed the same pattern, increasing from 39 percent to 74 percent. Among people aged 35-44, usage more than doubled, going from 27 percent to 61 percent.

The older groups started from much lower levels. Only 15 percent of people aged 45-54 used mobile internet in 2018, but by 2023 the figure had reached 43 percent, which was an increase of 28 percentage points. The 55 and over group remained the least connected, with usage growing from just 6 percent to 24 percent. Nevertheless, this group still showed a fourfold rise over the five years.
band7.comment: Accurate and well organised, with a clear overview. The vocabulary is sound but a little repetitive in places.

band8.answer:
The bar chart illustrates the percentage of Bangladeshis in five age groups who accessed the internet through a mobile phone in 2018 and 2023.

Overall, mobile internet use increased in every age group, and the likelihood of going online fell steadily with age in both years. The most striking proportional growth occurred among older users, who began from a very low base.

Among 16 to 24 year olds, usage climbed from 48 percent to 82 percent, the highest figure in the chart. The 25-34 group rose from 39 percent to 74 percent, a rise of 35 points. A similarly steep rise was seen in the 35-44 group, where usage more than doubled from 27 percent to 61 percent.

Older people were considerably less connected. Usage among 45 to 54 year olds almost tripled, from 15 percent to 43 percent, a gain of 28 percentage points. The 55 and over category remained the lowest in both years, but it quadrupled from 6 percent to 24 percent. Even so, by 2023 this group trailed the youngest users by 58 percentage points.
band8.comment: Precise figures, calculated changes and a well-developed overview make a strong response. Language is varied and accurate.

title: The line graph below shows the number of passengers using three modes of public transport in a Bangladeshi city between 2004 and 2022.
instruction: Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
overview: Bus and train use generally rose apart from a sharp fall in 2020, while ferry use declined over most of the period.
key_features: Bus is the most used mode throughout
Ferry is the only mode below its 2004 level in 2022

band7.answer:
The line graph illustrates how many passengers per year used buses, trains and river ferries in a city in Bangladesh between 2004 and 2022, in millions.

Overall, buses were the most popular form of transport throughout the period. Bus and train use generally increased, apart from a sharp drop in 2020, while the number of ferry passengers fell over most of the period.

Bus passengers rose from 120 million in 2004 to 135 million in 2008, 150 million in 2012 and a peak of 170 million in 2016. Train use followed a similar pattern, increasing from 40 million to 58 million over the same years.

In 2020, all three modes recorded their lowest figures, with 110 million bus passengers, 31 million train passengers and 28 million ferry passengers. Buses and trains then recovered to 160 million and 55 million in 2022. Ferry use, which had fallen steadily from 60 million in 2004, only reached 38 million. In 2022, bus and train use remained slightly below their 2016 peaks, by 10 million and 3 million respectively.
band7.comment: The answer organises the data logically and includes a clear overview. More precise comparative language would improve it further.

band8.answer:
The line graph compares annual passenger numbers on buses, trains and river ferries in a Bangladeshi city between 2004 and 2022, measured in millions.

Overall, buses carried the most passengers throughout. Bus and train patronage grew until 2016 before a sudden dip in 2020 and a partial recovery, whereas ferry travel declined for most of the period.

In 2004, buses served 120 million passengers, three times the train figure of 40 million and twice the ferry total of 60 million. Bus use climbed steadily to peak at 170 million in 2016, while trains rose in parallel to 58 million.

All three modes were hit in 2020, when bus numbers fell to 110 million, trains to 31 million and ferries to 28 million. Thereafter, buses rebounded to 160 million and trains to 55 million by 2022, both close to their previous highs. Ferries, by contrast, had already fallen from 60 million to 44 million by 2016 and managed only a modest recovery to 38 million. In total, the three modes carried 220 million passengers in 2004 and 253 million in 2022.
band8.comment: Precise ratios and a well-judged contrast between recovering and declining modes show strong data selection. The structure is clear and cohesive.

title: The line graph below shows the percentage of adults who smoked daily in three age groups between 1995 and 2020.
overview: Daily smoking fell in all three age groups, most steeply among the youngest, so that the oldest group ended with the highest rate.

band7.answer:
The line graph illustrates the proportion of adults who smoked every day in three age groups between 1995 and 2020.

Overall, smoking rates decreased in all three groups, but the fall was far greater among younger adults. As a result, people aged 50 and over had the highest rate by 2020, having started with the lowest.

In 1995, the 30-49 group had the highest smoking rate at 38 per cent, followed by the 18-29 group at 32 per cent and those aged 50 and over at 28 per cent. The 30-49 figure fell slowly to 34 per cent in 2005 and then more quickly, reaching 20 per cent in 2020.

The decline was most dramatic among 18-29 year olds. Their rate dropped from 32 per cent to 26 per cent in 2005, and then to just 12 per cent in 2020, the lowest figure on the chart. By contrast, the oldest group changed very little. It rose slightly to 29 per cent in 2000 before easing gradually to 23 per cent in 2020, which was above the other two groups.
band7.comment: The overview highlights the reversal in ranking, and figures are accurate. Language is appropriate but could show greater range.

band8.answer:
The line graph shows what percentage of adults smoked daily in three age brackets over a twenty-five-year period, from 1995 to 2020.

Overall, daily smoking declined in every age group, but the reduction was much steeper among younger adults, with the result that those aged 50 and over, who began with the lowest rate, ended with the highest.

In 1995, adults aged 30 to 49 were the heaviest smokers at 38 per cent, ahead of the 18-29 group on 32 per cent and the oldest group on 28 per cent. The middle group's rate slipped gently to 37 per cent in 2000 and 34 per cent in 2005, then fell faster to 30, 25 and finally 20 per cent in 2020.

Young adults experienced the most pronounced fall. Their figure dropped consistently, from 32 to 30, 26, 21 and 16 per cent, before bottoming out at 12 per cent, just over a third of the original level. In contrast, smoking among those aged 50 and over remained relatively stable, peaking at 29 per cent in 2000 and then easing to 25 per cent in 2010 and 23 per cent in 2020.
band8.comment: Sophisticated overview, precise figures and effective use of comparative language such as ratios and rankings. Cohesion is smooth across paragraphs.

title: The bar chart below shows the average one-way commuting time to work in five Bangladeshi cities in 2005 and 2023.
overview: Commuting times increased in all five cities, with Dhaka the longest and showing by far the largest rise.

band7.answer:
The bar chart compares the average time that workers spent travelling one way to work in five cities in Bangladesh in 2005 and 2023.

Overall, commuting times became longer in every city. Dhaka had the longest journeys in both years, and it also experienced the largest increase, while the smaller cities saw only modest changes.

In 2005, a typical commuter in Dhaka spent 35 minutes travelling to work, but by 2023 this had risen to 62 minutes, an increase of 27 minutes. Chattogram showed a similar though smaller trend, with the average journey growing from 28 minutes to 45 minutes.

The other three cities had much shorter commutes. In Khulna, the time increased from 20 to 26 minutes, and in Rajshahi it went up from 18 to 22 minutes, which was the smallest rise in the chart. Sylhet began with the shortest journey, at 17 minutes, but its figure climbed to 25 minutes by 2023, overtaking Rajshahi. As a result, the gap between Dhaka and the other cities widened considerably over the period.
band7.comment: Good coverage of main trends with accurate data. Some phrases are repeated, which limits the lexical score slightly.

band8.answer:
The bar chart shows how long the average one-way journey to work took in five Bangladeshi cities in 2005 and in 2023.

Overall, commuting times lengthened in all five cities, but the increase was far more dramatic in the two largest urban centres. Dhaka recorded the longest journeys in both years, whereas Rajshahi and Khulna remained relatively stable.

In Dhaka, the typical commute almost doubled, from 35 minutes in 2005 to 62 minutes in 2023, an extra 27 minutes. Chattogram experienced a considerable rise as well, with journey times growing from 28 to 45 minutes, a difference of 17 minutes.

By contrast, changes elsewhere were marginal. Khulna's average edged up from 20 to 26 minutes, and Rajshahi's from 18 to 22 minutes. Sylhet, which had the shortest commute in 2005 at 17 minutes, saw a rise of 8 minutes to 25 minutes and therefore overtook Rajshahi. By 2023, a Dhaka commuter spent more than twice as long travelling as someone in Khulna or Rajshahi, so the capital's congestion clearly stands apart from the other cities.
band8.comment: Excellent selection and comparison of key data with accurate calculations. The range of structures and vocabulary is wide and natural.

title: The line graph below shows the percentage of adults with diabetes in three age groups in Bangladesh between 2000 and 2020.
instruction: Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
overview: Diabetes became more common in every age group, and the older the group, the higher the rate throughout.
key_features: All three groups rise over 20 years
Oldest group has the highest rate each year
Middle group shows the fastest growth

band7.answer:
The line graph shows the percentage of adults with diabetes in three age groups in Bangladesh over a twenty-year period from 2000 to 2020.

Overall, the rate of diabetes rose in all three groups. The oldest group had the highest rate in every year, while the youngest group had the lowest, and the gap between the groups widened.

Among people aged 60 and over, the figure rose from 12 percent in 2000 to 16 percent in 2005 and 20 percent in 2010. It then reached 25 percent in 2015 and 27 percent in 2020, the highest value on the graph.

The 40 to 59 age group showed a similar upward trend, climbing from 8 percent to 11 percent, 14 percent and 17 percent, before reaching 20 percent in 2020. In contrast, the rate for those aged 20 to 39 grew only slightly, from 3 percent in 2000 to 7 percent in 2020, so it remained far below the other groups.
band7.comment: The overview is clear and the figures are used accurately. The writing would benefit from more calculated comparisons between the groups.

band8.answer:
The line graph compares the proportion of adults suffering from diabetes in three age categories in Bangladesh at five-year intervals from 2000 to 2020.

Overall, prevalence increased in every category, and the likelihood of having diabetes was consistently higher among older people, with the differences between groups becoming more pronounced.

The oldest group, aged 60 and above, started at 12 percent and rose by 4 points every five years until 2010, when it hit 20 percent. Growth then eased to 5 points and finally 2 points, leaving the figure at 27 percent in 2020.

The middle group experienced the most dramatic proportional change, rising from 8 percent to 20 percent, a 2.5-fold increase, with an increase of 3 points in each interval. Meanwhile, the youngest group saw only a gradual climb of 1 point every five years, from 3 percent to 7 percent, and in 2020 its rate was less than a third of that of the over-60s. The 2020 gap between the oldest and youngest groups was 20 percentage points, compared with just 9 points in 2000, which shows how unevenly the burden has grown.
band8.comment: The calculations are accurate and give real analytical depth to the description. Complex sentences are controlled and the vocabulary is precise.

title: The bar chart below shows the average number of hours per week that people in five age groups spent using smartphones and computers.
overview: Smartphones were used more than computers in every age group, with usage of both devices peaking among young adults.

band7.answer:
The bar chart compares the average weekly time spent on smartphones and computers by people in five age groups.

Overall, smartphones were used for longer than computers in every age group. Usage of both devices was highest among young adults and lowest among people aged 50 and over.

The 18-24 group spent the most time on smartphones, at 22 hours per week, followed by the 25-34 group at 19 hours and the 10-17 group at 14 hours. Those aged 35-49 used phones for 13 hours, while the figure for the oldest group was only 8 hours.

Computer use showed a similar pattern, but the numbers were lower. People aged 25-34 spent the longest on computers, at 15 hours, which was just 4 hours less than their smartphone use and the smallest gap among all groups. The 18-24 group followed with 11 hours, and those aged 35-49 used a computer for 10 hours. Computer use was much lower for the youngest group, at 6 hours, and the over-50s, at just 4 hours, which was half their smartphone time.
band7.comment: Accurate data, clear overview and logical grouping by device. A few more comparative structures would help reach Band 8.

band8.answer:
The bar chart illustrates how many hours per week people in five age brackets spent on smartphones and on computers.

Overall, smartphones took up more time than computers for every age group, and both devices were used most heavily by young adults, with the oldest group spending the least time on each.

Smartphone use peaked at 22 hours among 18 to 24 year olds, comfortably ahead of the 25-34 group on 19 hours. Teenagers aged 10 to 17 came next with 14 hours, marginally above the 35-49 group at 13 hours, while those aged 50 and over recorded just 8 hours.

Computer use followed a similar trend at a lower level. Adults aged 25 to 34 spent the longest on computers, at 15 hours, which was only 4 hours below their smartphone use, the narrowest gap in the chart. The figures for the 18-24 and 35-49 groups were 11 and 10 hours respectively. The youngest and oldest groups used computers least, at 6 and 4 hours. For the over-50s, this was exactly half of their smartphone time.

band7.answer:
The diagram illustrates how jute plants are turned into sacks in Bangladesh, and there are eight stages in total.

Overall, the process begins with the harvesting of the plants in the field and ends with the production of finished sacks, and it moves from natural preparation to factory manufacturing.

First, the jute plants are harvested, and the stems are tied into bundles. These bundles are then soaked in water, which is known as retting, so that the fibres loosen. After that, the fibres are stripped from the stems and washed, and they are dried in the sun.

Once dry, the fibres are graded according to quality and packed into bales. Next, they are softened and spun into yarn. The yarn is then woven into cloth on looms. Finally, the cloth is cut into the required size and sewn into sacks. In this way, the plant material is gradually changed from a raw crop into a strong, usable product. The early stages take place in the countryside, whereas the later ones are carried out in a mill or factory.

Once dried, the fibres are sorted by grade and compressed into bales for transport. At the mill, they are softened and spun into yarn, which is then woven into strong cloth. In the final stage, the cloth is cut to size and stitched together to form sacks. The sequence therefore divides into two broad phases. instruction: Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

steps: Dung mixed with water to make slurry
Slurry fed into an airtight digester
Bacteria break down slurry without oxygen
Gas collects in a storage dome
Gas piped to the kitchen stove
Leftover slurry dried and used as fertiliser

overview: Biogas production has seven stages, producing cooking gas and a useful fertiliser from the same waste.
key_features: Airtight digester is the central stage
Two useful outputs: gas and fertiliser

band7.answer:
The diagram shows how cow dung is used to produce biogas for cooking in a village home in Bangladesh, and it has seven stages.

Overall, the process turns animal waste into two useful products, which are cooking gas and fertiliser.

At the start of the process, cow dung is collected and then mixed with water to make a slurry. This mixture is fed into an airtight digester. Inside the digester, bacteria break down the slurry without oxygen, and this produces gas.

The gas rises and collects in a storage dome above the digester. After that, it is piped to the stove in the kitchen, where it is burned for cooking. Meanwhile, the slurry that is left over is removed from the digester, dried and used as fertiliser on the fields. The two outputs are produced in different ways. The gas is the direct result of the bacterial action in the digester, while the fertiliser is made from the slurry that remains. As a result, almost nothing from the original dung is wasted in the process.
band7.comment: The process is described in the correct order, and the overview identifies both outputs. Some sentences are repetitive and could be more varied.

band8.answer:
The diagram illustrates the seven stages involved in generating biogas from cow dung at a rural household in Bangladesh.

Overall, the system converts livestock waste into two valuable outputs, namely cooking fuel and fertiliser, and the digester is at the centre of the process.

To begin with, cow dung is gathered and combined with water to form a slurry, which is then fed into a sealed, airtight digester. Within this chamber, bacteria decompose the slurry in the absence of oxygen, releasing gas as a by-product.

The gas accumulates in a dome-shaped storage chamber and is subsequently piped directly to the kitchen stove, where it is used as fuel. In the meantime, the residue left in the digester is removed and dried, after which it is spread on crops as fertiliser. It is worth noting that the process yields two outputs from a single input. The gas comes from the bacterial breakdown of the slurry, whereas the fertiliser is the solid material that remains afterwards, so almost none of the original dung is wasted. The digester is therefore the central stage, as every later stage depends on what happens inside it.
band8.comment: Accurate passive forms and varied linking phrases create smooth progression. The explanation of both outputs in the overview adds clarity.

title: The pie chart below shows how university students in Bangladesh spent their time online in 2023.
overview: Students spent most of their online time on social media, with study and video streaming also significant and shopping minor.
key_features: Social media largest at 34 per cent
Shopping and other under 10 per cent combined

band7.answer:
The pie chart illustrates how university students in Bangladesh divided their online time among six activities in 2023.

Overall, social media took up the largest share of students' time online, followed by study and research. Online shopping and other activities accounted for the smallest proportions.

Social media was the most popular activity, at 34 per cent of total time, which was 8 percentage points higher than study and research at 26 per cent. Together, these two activities made up 60 per cent of everything students did online.

Video streaming came third, at 20 per cent, so one fifth of the total. Online gaming accounted for a further 12 per cent. The two remaining categories were far smaller. Students spent only 5 per cent of their time on online shopping, and 3 per cent on other activities. Combined, these two categories accounted for just 8 per cent, which was less than the share of gaming alone. This shows that entertainment and communication dominated the online habits of the students.
band7.comment: Accurate figures with simple, clear grouping and a sound overview. Range of vocabulary for proportion is adequate but limited.

band8.answer:
The pie chart shows the distribution of university students' online time in Bangladesh across six categories in 2023.

Overall, social media absorbed the biggest portion of students' time online, while study and research came a clear second. Shopping and miscellaneous uses were minor activities by comparison.

Social media accounted for 34 per cent of total online time, slightly more than a third and 8 percentage points above study and research, which made up 26 per cent. Between them, these two categories represented 60 per cent of all online activity.

Entertainment-related uses made up most of the remainder. Video streaming constituted exactly one fifth of the total, and online gaming took a further 12 per cent. The remaining categories were marginal. Online shopping was the choice of only 5 per cent of students' time, and other activities were 3 per cent. These last two combined came to 8 per cent, which was lower than gaming alone, and well under a quarter of the share taken by social media and study together.
band8.comment: Precise percentages, well-chosen combined figures and fluent complex sentences. The overview and the closing comparison show strong analytical selection.

title: The table below shows the number of passengers who used four forms of public transport in Bangladesh in 2015, 2020 and 2023.
overview: Bus travel was far more popular than any other mode and grew steadily, while domestic air was the smallest and most volatile.
key_features: Air falls then recovers above its 2015 level

band7.answer:
The table compares the number of passengers, in millions, who travelled by four types of public transport in Bangladesh in 2015, 2020 and 2023.

Overall, buses carried far more passengers than any other form of transport, and their numbers grew throughout the period. Domestic air travel was the least used mode, although it showed the most noticeable change in percentage terms.

In 2015, 420 million passengers used buses, and this rose to 510 million in 2020 and 590 million in 2023. Rail travel also increased steadily, from 58 million to 62 million and then to 71 million, but it remained much lower than the bus figures.

Inland waterways carried 95 million passengers in 2015, which fell slightly to 88 million in 2020 before recovering to 92 million in 2023. This meant that waterway use ended the period a little below where it started. Domestic air travel was very small. It attracted 3.1 million passengers in 2015, fell to 1.8 million in 2020, and then rose to 4.6 million in 2023, which was higher than the starting figure.
band7.comment: Accurate reporting of all four modes with a good overview. A little more comparison between modes would improve the score.

band8.answer:
The table illustrates how many passengers used four public transport modes in Bangladesh in 2015, 2020 and 2023, in millions.

Overall, buses were overwhelmingly the most popular mode and attracted steadily growing numbers, whereas domestic air travel remained marginal despite considerable fluctuation. Inland waterways were the only mode to end the period slightly below its starting level.

Bus passengers rose from 420 million in 2015 to 510 million in 2020 and then to 590 million in 2023, an overall increase of 170 million. By 2023 buses carried more than eight times as many passengers as rail, which itself grew modestly from 58 million to 62 million and finally 71 million.

Waterway travel was more erratic. It slipped from 95 million to 88 million between 2015 and 2020 before recovering to 92 million. Domestic air travel recorded the smallest figures, dropping from 3.1 million to 1.8 million in 2020, probably reflecting the disruption of that year, before climbing to 4.6 million in 2023, nearly 50 percent above its 2015 level and its highest figure in the table.
band8.comment: Detailed, accurate and well-organised with sound calculations. The answer shows a wide range of vocabulary and complex structures.

title: The diagram below shows how used plastic bottles are recycled into new plastic products.
instruction: Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

steps: Bottles sorted by type and colour
Bottles washed to remove labels and dirt
Pellets sold to factories for new products

overview: Recycling has seven stages, moving from collection and cleaning to melting and the sale of pellets.

band7.answer:
The diagram shows the process of recycling used plastic bottles into new plastic goods. There are seven stages in total.

Overall, the bottles are collected, cleaned and broken down, and are then melted and turned into pellets, which are sold to manufacturers.

First, the used bottles are collected, and they are sorted according to their type and colour. They are then washed to remove labels and dirt. Next, the clean bottles are shredded into small flakes by a machine.

In the following stage, the flakes are melted at a high temperature. The molten plastic is cut into small pellets, which is the last stage of the recycling itself. Finally, the pellets are sold to factories, where they are used to make new plastic products. In summary, the process includes four preparation stages, which are collection, sorting, washing and shredding, followed by two stages in which the plastic is melted and shaped, and a final sale stage. Washing is carried out before shredding so that dirt and labels do not contaminate the melted plastic.
band7.comment: The stages are in the right order and the passive is used well. The sentences are fairly simple, so greater variety would help.

band8.answer:
The diagram illustrates how discarded plastic bottles are recycled into raw material for new products, in seven stages.

Overall, the process moves from collection and cleaning through to melting and pelletising, and the end product is sold to manufacturers instead of being a finished item.

Initially, used bottles are collected and sorted by type and colour. They are subsequently washed to remove labels and dirt before being shredded into small flakes.

Once the flakes have been produced, they are melted at a high temperature, and the molten plastic is cut into uniform pellets. In the final stage, these pellets are sold to factories, where they serve as the raw material for making new plastic products. In summary, the seven stages fall into three groups. The first four, which are collection, sorting, washing and shredding, prepare the material. The next two, melting and cutting, change its physical form, and the last stage, sale to factories, delivers the pellets to manufacturers. Washing precedes shredding so that dirt and labels are removed while the bottles are still whole.
band8.comment: The answer shows excellent control of passive and sequencing structures. The overview notes that the pellets are an intermediate product, which shows good understanding of the diagram.
